## What the evidence shows

**Changes (7-day lookback, 2026-08-26 → alert):** exactly one recorded change to io-shop — a deploy at `2026-09-02T21:34:00Z`, revision `9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e`, actor `kuki`, from the k8s production config repo. No feature-flag toggles anywhere in the week.

**Timing:** the deploy lands at 21:34, the minute the metrics are still at baseline (p95 220ms, err 0.01). The very next minute p95 jumps to 900ms and the logs say "p95 latency climbing"; it monotonically degrades to 1800ms then 5000ms timeouts with error rate 0.12. The degradation is latency-led with request volume flat/slightly falling (1150 → 1050), i.e. not load-driven.

hypotheses.subject: 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e
hypotheses.summary: The deploy of revision 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e at 21:34 introduced a latency regression in io-shop: p95 rose from a 220ms baseline through 900ms and 1800ms to 5000ms timeouts within three minutes of the rollout, driving error rate from 0.01 to 0.12 while traffic was flat.
supporting_evidence: Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-08-26T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-02T21:37:33Z. [ ...one deploy only... ]
2026-09-02T21:36:00Z WARN io-shop: p95 latency at 1800ms, up from a 220ms baseline

hypotheses.summary: No cause is established beyond the coincidence in time. The only artefact in view is a deploy one minute before onset; the logs contain nothing about what the new revision did (no dependency, pool, GC or query detail), and no rollback observation confirms the deploy was at fault. A saturating downstream dependency or resource exhaustion would produce the same latency-led, volume-flat signature.
